title: "Python interface"

This document describes the design of the Python functions forming the CLI and
the library layer, as well as tracking implementation status.

{{< include /docs/includes/_design-status.qmd >}}

## CLI

### {{< var done >}} `extract_metadata()`

`extract_metadata()` has two arguments: `parquet_path` and `output_path`. The
`parquet_path` argument is the path to a Parquet file in, e.g. the `staging/`
directory, and the `output_path` argument is the path to the Python script that
will have the `ResourceProperties()` dataclass filled in with the extracted
metadata.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow-extract-resource-metadata
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of objects and functions to extract a resource's
%%|   metadata from data.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   A flow diagram showing the steps to extract resource metadata from a
%%|   Parquet file.

flowchart
    parquet[/"Parquet data<br>[PARQUET-PATH]"/]
    read_parquet["read_parquet()"]
    output_opt[/"Output path<br>[--output]"/]
    output[/"Python script<br>[File]"/]
    data[("DataFrame<br>(Tidy)")]
    extract_metadata["extract_column_metadata()"]
    metadata[("ResourceProperties<br>(extracted)")]
    init_metadata["init_resource_metadata()"]

    parquet --> read_parquet
    read_parquet --> data
    data --> extract_metadata
    extract_metadata --> metadata -->|render<br>from<br>template| init_metadata
    output_opt --> write["write_file()"]
    init_metadata -->|string| write
    write --> output
```

### {{< var done >}} `init_metadata()`

`init_metadata()` has two arguments: `output_path` and `type`. The `output_path`
argument is the path to where the Python script will be created, which will
contain an empty `PackageProperties()` or `ResourceProperties()` dataclass. The
`type` argument is the type of metadata to create: `package` or `resource`.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow-init-metadata
%%| fig-cap: >-
%%|   Diagram showing the flow of objects and functions to compose the metadata
%%|   in a Python script.
%%| fig-alt: >-
%%|   A flow diagram showing the steps to creating the Python file with the
%%|   empty metadata fields.

flowchart
    output_path[/"Output path<br>[output_path]"/]
    type[/"Type of metadata<br>[type]"/]
    template[/"Template<br>[File]"/]
    init_metadata["init_*_metadata()"]
    write_file("write_file()")
    output[/"Python script<br>[File]"/]

    type -->|package<br>or resource| init_metadata
    template --> init_metadata -->|string| write_file
    output_path --> write_file --> output
```

### {{< var planned >}} `build-resources`

The `build-resources` command converts sets of staged Parquet files into the
final resources.

If any step errors, the build stops immediately without any cleanup. The
displaying of errors is handled by `run_without_tracebacks()` from Soil. It is
the responsibility of each internal function raising the error to include enough
information in the message to identify the point of failure (e.g., which
resource failed at which step).

<!-- TODO: Decide if no batches for a resource is an error. -->
<!-- TODO: Decide whether to normalise data types before concat and join (batches and deleted IDs can disagree even when each matches the metadata). -->

The following classes are used to represent the resources throughout the build
pipeline:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Batch:
    """The data from one staged file, with the timestamp taken from its file name."""

    path: Path
    timestamp: datetime
    data: pl.LazyFrame


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BuildTarget:
    """The build details for one resource, including where to read and write it."""

    resource_metadata: ResourceProperties
    input_dir: Path
    output_path: Path


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BuildData[T]:
    """A resource's build target together with its data at one stage of the build."""

    build_target: BuildTarget
    data: T
```

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-cap: >-

%%|   command.
%%| fig-alt: >-

%%|   `build-resources` CLI command.

flowchart TD
    %% Config and metadata
    config_file[/"config_file"/]:::io --> read_config["read_config()<br><i>raises if not found or incorrect</i>"] --> Config[/"Config"/]
    project_dir[/"project_dir"/]:::io --> read_config
    Config -->|metadata_file| read_metadata["read_metadata()<br><i>raises if not found or incorrect</i>"] --> metadata[/"PackageMetadata"/]
    project_dir --> read_metadata
    metadata --> check_metadata["check_metadata()<br><i>raises if incorrect</i>"] --> metadata_checked[/"PackageMetadata"/]

    %% Deleted IDs
    Config -->|delete_obs_units_file| read_csv["pl.read_csv()<br><i>may raise</i>"] --> deleted_ids[/"pl.DataFrame"/]
    project_dir --> read_csv
    metadata_checked --> check_deleted_ids["check_deleted_ids()<br><i>raises if incorrect</i>"] --> deleted_ids_checked[/"pl.DataFrame"/]
    deleted_ids --> check_deleted_ids

    %% Resources: each step runs over the whole list
    Config -->|resources| resource_configs[/"list[ResourceConfig]"/]
    resource_configs --> get_build_target["get_build_target()<br><i>raises if resource missing</i>"] --> build_targets[/"list[BuildTarget]"/]
    project_dir --> get_build_target
    metadata_checked --> get_build_target

    build_targets --> read_staged_resource["read_staged_resource()<br><i>raises if timestamp incorrect</i>"] --> staged[/"list[BuildData[list[Batch]]]"/]
    staged --> check_schema["check_schema()<br><i>raises if incorrect</i>"]
    check_schema --> join_batches["join_batches()"]
    join_batches --> joined[/"list[BuildData[pl.LazyFrame]]"/]

    joined --> drop_deleted_ids["drop_deleted_ids()"] --> joined_after_delete[/"list[BuildData[pl.LazyFrame]]"/]
    deleted_ids_checked -->|"if any"| drop_deleted_ids
    joined_after_delete --> collect["collect()<br><i>errors on lazy frames surface here</i>"]

    collect --> collected[/"list[BuildData[pl.DataFrame]]"/]
    collected --> check_constraints["check_constraints()<br><i>raises if incorrect</i>"]
    check_constraints --> write_parquet["write_parquet()<br><i>may raise</i>"]
    write_parquet --> outputs[/"output Parquet files"/]:::io

    classDef io fill:#FFF
```

## Library

### {{< var done >}} Metadata classes

These classes contain an explicit, structured set of official metadata defined
for a data package. The main purpose of these classes is to give programmatic
access to the structured metadata. That way the metadata can be generated from
writing Python code that, if it's possible, can processes some input source of
metadata into Sprout's metadata structure. The classes also make it easier to
get an overview or learn about what fields are part of the metadata in Sprout
(e.g. optional vs required fields) and what will be eventually generated into
the final data package. We currently only have metadata classes for the [Data
Package spec](https://datapackage.org).

See the help documentation with `help(SproutProperties())` for more details on
the metadata classes.
